thallgren
body:
Eviction might be prevented when a disruption budget is in place because Kubernetes will not start a new pod until after the eviction. This commit introduces three ways to mitigate this problem.

1. When multiple evictions are made, and some of those evictions have succeeded, then a good strategy is to just wait until the evicted pods are recreated, and then continue to evict others.
2. For a deployment or argo-rollout, applying a patch with a restart annotation causes all pods to be redeployed in a manner that doesn't disrupt the budget.
3. For replicasets and statefulsets, the approach is to scale up above the budget threshold, evict the pod, and then scale back down again.

author: chansuke
body:
Fix #4122. 

This reverts commit 2e7cf6932a0c5111967d6ba4b27716580985a34f.

I encountered the same issue in production on `v1.8.0` and identified the problematic commit using `git bisect`:

```
git bisect start
git bisect good v1.7.2
git bisect bad v1.8.0
```

I then verified the regression locally by running:

```
docker build --target kubectl-argo-rollouts -t kubectl-argo-rollouts:test .
docker run -p 3100:3100 kubectl-argo-rollouts:test dashboard
```

The upgrade to react-scripts v5.0.1 includes [breaking changes](https://github.com/facebook/create-react-app/releases/tag/v5.0.0) that affect performance. While I have not yet pinpointed the exact cause of the [regression](https://github.com/facebook/create-react-app/releases/tag/v5.0.0), reverting to react-scripts `v4.0.3` immediately restores performance.

Since [v5.0.1](https://github.com/facebook/create-react-app/releases/tag/v5.0.1) is the latest `create-react-app` release and is already 3 years old, I am also considering migrating to [Vite](https://vite.dev/) as a long-term solution for improved performance.

author: rexskz
body:
# Fix an edge case

There will be a panic when `m.Left == -1`, this is the root cause of this issue.

The reason why `m.Left == -1` is due to the `exact_month_date` rule that returns an empty string for `这周三` (this Wednesday).

But simply fixing this issue will cause another issue ↓

# Fix Chinese `exact_month_date` rule

The previous regex will recognise `2下周天` as `2`.

- This is "a normal number `2` and `next Sunday`", which should be `next Sunday`, since `2` is meaningless here.
- A regex will match `2`, which is wrong.
- I separated the "number-only form" from the "number & Chinese character form" to fix this issue.
- To prevent the regex from returning an empty string, the "number-only form" should be placed first.

---

Close #47

To start a local version of the demo follow the instructions below. 

1. Ensure that you have docker installed on your machine. If you do not have docker see the _setting up docker section_ below. 
2. Navigate to the /root of the project
3. Run `Docker compose up` this will build the necessary containers. Caution: This step will take considerable time on initial build.
4. Once your upload database with DB file 'Need to Add file'
5. To restore from a backup run the command `cat <backup-file-name.sql> | docker exec -i postgres psql -U postgres` 
The most recent backup is located here: **_db_backups/pgsql_backup_2025-04-16.sql**
All backups are authored to the `_db_backups/` folder, replace the <backup-file-name.sql> in the script with the most recently authored file. 
6. To Create a backup of your postgres DB run the command `yarn db-gen-backup` 

## Running Strapi:

Assuming that the containers were built successfully from the previous step you can begin to interface with the strapi ui 

1.  You might be prompted with one of 2 setup interfaces,  
2. If you are presented with a standard login screen, the login credentials are the following: 
**Username**: smalone@element84.com

_*Be sure to retain these credentials in some manner. If they are lost you will need to delete the docker volumes, image, and container, and rebuild strapi_

4.  Once logged in, you can start your local version of the front-end. Open an additional terminal window at the /root of the project run `yarn dev`

## What

Update `ContentItem#contributors` so that it returns a list of contributor content item objects rather than an array of hashed link values.

## Why

The hashes are presentational (they're to be passed into the govuk_styled_links_list helper method), so better that they're in presenter code. author: maciejmakowski2003
body:
<!-- Reference any GitHub issues resolved by this PR -->

Closes #333 

## Introduced changes

<!-- A brief description of the changes -->

- Removed `StretcherNode` from native side. All time-stretching and pitch-shifting features were moved to `AudioBufferSourceNode`. Currently setting `AudioBufferSourceNode.timeStretch = 'speech-music'` enables using pitch-correction algorithm while changing `playbackRate`. In addition `detune` in this mode is responsible for pitch-shifting.
- Added `onended` event to `ABSN` that allows to get pause time.
- Refactored time-stretch lib and whole dsp utiles.

Files with breaking changes:
- AudioFile
- HostObjects of ABSN, AudioContext, BaseAudioContext, AudioScheduledSourceNode
- ABSN, AudioScheduledSourceNode, OscillatorNode, PeriodicWave, AnalyserNode

author: jrmhaig
body:
#### What

Bug fix; When two messages are submitted on a claim without fully reloading the page the second message does not get displayed automatically.

#### Ticket

[CCCD - Failure to refresh messages after submitting](https://dsdmoj.atlassian.net/browse/CTSKF-1106)

#### Why

A Javascript error prevents the page from being updated fully meaning that, although a message has been created and added to a claim, it does not appear on the page. This causes confusion for the user and results in multiple duplicate messages being created.

#### How

The error results from a constant being created in the global scope each time a message is submitted. As a constant cannot be redefined this results in a fatal error the second and subsequent times this is executed. To fix, this code is moved inside the `processMsg` method in `moj.Modules.Messaging`.

_Created new PR to re-run the tests and remove 2x merge commits from the PR. Old PR #21887_ 

#### Why I did it

Added Dynamic Port Breakout support for the DELL S5232F-ON.

#### Related issue

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/21315

#### How I did it

- Created ``device/dell/x86_64-dellemc_s5232f_c3538-r0/DellEMC-S5232f-C32/hwsku.json``
- Created ``device/dell/x86_64-dellemc_s5232f_c3538-r0/platform.json``
- Modified ``device/dell/x86_64-dellemc_s5232f_c3538-r0/DellEMC-S5232f-C32/td3-s5232f-32x100G.config.bcm``

#### How to verify it

1. Install the SONiC branch ``202411`` on a S5232F-ON.
2. Take the new files (``hwsku.json``, ``platform.json`` and ``td3-s5232f-32x100G.config.bcm``) from my commit: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/tree/b5d81ea1ec52d012d33238949f9a2d7b8c276236/device/dell/x86_64-dellemc_s5232f_c3538-r0 and move them to your SONiC installation.
3. Move ``platform.json`` to this path: ``/usr/share/sonic/device/x86_64-dellemc_s5232f_c3538-r0/``
4. Replace ``td3-s5232f-32x100G.config.bcm`` to this path: ``/usr/share/sonic/device/x86_64-dellemc_s5232f_c3538-r0/DellEMC-S5232f-C32/``
5. Move ``hwsku.json`` to this path: ``/usr/share/sonic/device/x86_64-dellemc_s5232f_c3538-r0/DellEMC-S5232f-C32/``
6. Restart the switch ``sudo reboot``.
7. Check if ``show interfaces breakout`` returns an output.
8. Attempt to breakout a port, e.g. ``sudo config interface breakout Ethernet0 4x25G[10G]``
9. Check the interfaces status: ``sudo show interfaces status``

#### Tested branch (Please provide the tested image version)

- [x] 202411

#### Description for the changelog
Added Dynamic Breakout Support for DELL S5232F-ON:
- Created ``hwsku.json``
- Created ``platform.json``
- Modified: ``td3-s5232f-32x100G.config.bcm``

body:
## 🧰 Changes

Stumbled upon this while updating `oas` over in [api](https://npm.im/api) but the response typings on `Operation.getResponseAsJSONSchema()`, a `SchemaObject`, do not line up with what's actually being returned.

I _think_ that this slipped through because are aren't running in TS strict mode and the `jsonSchema` array we're composing is being  created as `any[]`. Then again, even without strict mode I don't understand how TS could see `any[]` and think that validates as `SchemaObject`.

Regardless, this fixes it up!

When it comes to dinner parties, the conversation is one thing that can’t be set up in advance. But that doesn’t mean you can’t be prepared. With the holiday season imminent, we asked Rico Gagliano and Brendan Francis Newnam, hosts of the podcast “The Dinner Party Download<\/a>,” for some dos and don’ts on how to spark memorable conversation during your dinner party.<\/p>

These tips are part of the magazine’s latest food issue all about the art of the dinner party<\/a>. Check it out for more inspiration and recipes to help you host your own dinner parties this season.<\/p>

Warm Up the Crowd<\/h2>

Small talk gives guests a chance to get to know one another, and to take one another’s measure, before the conversation turns to weightier matters — e.g., sex, the lonely meaninglessness of existence and Trump’s latest tweet. It’s like stretching before a jog.<\/p>

Be a Conversation Conduit<\/h2>

Don’t leave some guests nodding their heads and pretending they know what’s going on. Often, clarification is required. If a guest is mumbling, restate a phrase for people who couldn’t hear what was said. If a guest makes an inside joke, go ahead and laugh — and then put it in context for everyone.<\/p><\/div>

<\/aside><\/div>

Less Talking, More Listening<\/h2>

The sad truth is, no one cares what you have to say; they care about what they<\/em> have to say. Deep down, people want to feel they’ve been heard. They will if you let them talk.<\/p><\/div>

<\/aside><\/div>Samin Nosrat’s dinner party<\/a>

Embrace Complicated Topics<\/h2>

We all know what society says we’re not supposed to talk about at a dinner party. Religion. Politics. Salaries. And yet these topics should be fair game. What’s a dinner party if not a laboratory of ideas, plus permission to eat cheese?<\/p>

Provocation With Style<\/h2>

Don’t worry about dangerous conversational territory. The most memorable conversations are a product of guests who dare to provoke, titillate and argue. The trick is to create a permissive atmosphere with civility and style. The goal, Elaine Stritch once told us, is to be a “ladylike broad”: half civilized charmer, half wisecracking bomb-thrower.<\/p>

Keep Arguments Low-Key<\/h2>

A single conversation will not convince a lifelong liberal that it’s O.K. to own an arsenal of assault rifles. The perfect retort will not convince a conservative that we should be taxed to fund performance art. Accept this. It’s amazing how much more relaxed a political argument becomes when you understand that you don’t have to — and in fact won’t — “win.”<\/p><\/div>

<\/aside><\/div>

Personalize Your Politics<\/h2>

Go for empathy when you talk politics. Showing how a political issue affects you intimately is more important than data and statistics. Try leading with a personal story.<\/p>

The Two W’s: What and Why<\/h2>

To ensure that a guest’s story becomes truly interesting, just ask two questions over and over: what and why. What exactly happened? What did that feel like? Seek emotional specifics. And then: Why? Why is this anecdote important? This is where the guest’s most thoughtful connection to a story lies.<\/p>

Venture Into the Unconventional<\/h2>

Small talk need not be soporific. Before the dinner party, try to find some recent news items or weird science stories that people most likely haven’t heard about. Did you know that music is beneficial to cats undergoing surgery? Or that there is a library in Norway that is amassing 100 never-before-read books that no one can check out for 100 years?<\/p>

Don’t Assume<\/h2>

Asking questions can get a guest to reveal something fascinating about herself. But a quick way to prevent that is to give her possible answers. “Why did you quit law school — was it too boring?<\/em>” Leave out the guess. A short question is more likely to provoke details.<\/p><\/div>

body:
### Description
This PR introduces multi-instance support for the Sanity SDK, allowing applications to connect to multiple Sanity projects simultaneously. This is currently only useful for documents and can be used by adding a `resourceId` to your document handle in the form of `document:projectId.dataset:documentId`. For example the following is how you would use 2 different resources for a `useDocument` hook:

```ts
const doc: DocumentHandle<Author> = {
  _type: 'author',
  _id: 'db06bc9e-4608-465a-9551-a10cef478037',
  resourceId: 'document:ppsg7ml5.test:db06bc9e-4608-465a-9551-a10cef478037',
}

const doc2: DocumentHandle<Dog> = {

  _id: 'acc11e96-1a01-4907-bd0e-e8347217cf2f',

- Modified authentication to use global tokens instead of project-specific tokens
- Added resource ID support to document operations for targeting specific instances
- Enhanced hooks to work with multiple instances through resource IDs
- Removed project-scoped authentication in favor of global auth

Note this also removes the concept of project level authentication, so the "project auth" section of the kitchensink was removed and now we just have "authorized" and "unauthorized".

author: davner
body:
### Summary of Changes:
- Implemented an exit strategy in `loop_process` by handling `None` commands to break.
- Modified `ETISubprocess.terminate()` to gracefully stop the process and close queues.
- Reset the singleton ETISubprocess instance on termination.
- Prevented zombie processes and orphaned multiprocessing forks in long-running applications like GOATS when shutting down.

Hello DRAGONS team!

We’ve observed lingering multiprocessing forks and resource trackers when running DRAGONS reductions in GOATS. These changes address the issue for long-running applications and improve resource management.

### Details:
These changes address an issue where DRAGONS’ `runr` process leaves behind zombie and orphaned multiprocessing forks when used in long-running applications like GOATS or Jupyter notebooks. The root cause is that DRAGONS relies on `atexit` for cleanup, but in environments where the interpreter is not explicitly exited (such as persistent Django applications or even Jupyter notebooks), `atexit` is never triggered. This results in lingering child processes that accumulate over time.

### `loop_process` Changes:
By ensuring `loop_process` can be cleanly exited, GOATS can properly terminate workers without having to force terminate.

### `ETISubprocess.terminate` Changes:
- Puts in `inQueue` `None` which cleanly breaks the `while True` loop.
- The process can possibly cleanly exit without force termination.
- The queues are now closed to free up system resources.
- The singleton instance is set to `None` to reset stale references.

### Note
If changes to the cleanup process, including resource deallocation and singleton resetting, are not desirable, please consider at minimum adding the ability to cleanly break out of `loop_process`. As it stands, GOATS has to force terminate this.

author: hrko
body:
### Overview

This PR introduces crucial changes to enhance the reliability and robustness of the locking mechanism. Specifically, it adds the functionality to make lock acquisition atomic and to periodically refresh the lock's expiration time. These changes reduce the risk of race conditions in concurrent environments, leading to more stable certificate management.

### Key Changes

#### 1. Atomic Lock Acquisition Logic:

-   In the previous implementation, checking for lock existence and creating the lock were separate steps, which could allow another process to acquire the lock in between.
-   The new implementation uses DynamoDB's `PutItem` operation with a `ConditionExpression` to make lock existence check and creation atomic.
-   By combining the `attribute_not_exists` and `ExpiresAt` conditions, the lock is only acquired if it does not exist or if it exists but has expired.
-   Furthermore, each lock is assigned a unique UUID (`LockID`), and the `UpdateItem` operation's `ConditionExpression` checks the `LockID` to ensure that only the lock created by itself can be updated.

#### 2. Periodic Lock Expiration Refresh:

-   The previous implementation had a fixed lock expiration time, which could lead to the lock expiring if the critical section took too long.
-   The new implementation starts a goroutine within the `Lock` method to periodically refresh the lock's expiration time at `LockRefreshInterval` (defaulting to `LockTimeout` / 3).
-   This ensures that the lock is held until the critical section's process is complete.

### Problems Solved and Benefits of the Changes

-   **Race Condition Prevention:** Atomic lock acquisition prevents race conditions where multiple processes attempt to acquire the lock simultaneously.
-   **Critical Section Protection:** Periodic lock refreshes prevent other instances from entering the critical section at the same time due to the lock expiring during the execution of the critical section. This prevents situations like:
    1.  An instance acquires the lock and enters the critical section.
    2.  The critical section's processing takes a long time, and the lock expires.
    3.  Another instance acquires the lock and enters the critical section simultaneously.
    4.  As a result, unexpected behavior occurs (for example, the certificate issuance process in the instance that first acquired the lock may stall).
-   **Improved Reliability:** A more robust locking mechanism improves the reliability of certificate acquisition and renewal processes.
-   **Improved Stability in Clustered Environments:**  More stable behavior is expected, especially in clustered environments where multiple application instances share DynamoDB.

Please let me know if you have any questions or concerns. I'm looking forward to your feedback and the opportunity to contribute to this project.

## Use Apache Mina SSHD 2.15.0

Eclipse JGit 7.2.0 needs Apache Mina SSHD 2.15.0.

The [mailing list](https://lists.apache.org/thread/zrt5l2oxgon83lrgr6jt05bvt824yqxz) announces the Feb 25, 2025 release of Apache Mina SSHD 2.15.0 with the following key features:

* [GH-606](https://github.com/apache/mina-sshd/issues/606) Support ML-KEM PQC hybrid key exchanges
* [GH-652](https://github.com/apache/mina-sshd/issues/652) New method KnownHostsServerKeyVerifier.handleRevokedKey()
* [SSHD-988](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SSHD-988) Support ed25519 keys via the Bouncy Castle library

Bug fixes include:

* [GH-618](https://github.com/apache/mina-sshd/issues/618) Fix reading an OpenSshCertificate from a Buffer
* [GH-626](https://github.com/apache/mina-sshd/issues/626) Enable Streaming.Async for ChannelDirectTcpip
* [GH-628](https://github.com/apache/mina-sshd/issues/628) SFTP: fix reading directories with trailing blanks in the name
* [GH-636](https://github.com/apache/mina-sshd/issues/636) Fix handling of unsupported key types in known_hosts file
* [GH-642](https://github.com/apache/mina-sshd/issues/642) Do not use SecureRandom.getInstanceString() due to possible entropy starvation (regression in 2.14.0)
* [GH-654](https://github.com/apache/mina-sshd/issues/654) Fix test dependency for assertj in sshd-contrib

Includes changes from other pull requests for convenience, including:

* https://github.com/jenkinsci/mina-sshd-api-plugin/pull/151

body: ## Contexte J'ai téléchargé le fichier geojson qui contient les formes et les données de pollution chaque année, et j'ai transformé les données en PMTiles (formes des communes + code INSEE uniquement) + CSV (code INSEE + données de chaque année): - Pour les formes des communes - Utilisez PMtiles - car le fichier de forme est volumineux mais statique, ce qui réduit la taille du chargement initial des données) - Pour les couleurs des communes (données de pollution) - Utiliser CSV (taille de fichier <600KB) avec les identifiants des communes - Colorier la commune en fonction du code INSEE de la commune et de l'état de la pollution en utilisant Maplibre Je pense qu'en séparant les données sur la pollution des PMTiles, nous pouvons avoir plus de flexibilité dans la modification des différents types de données (différentes années, nouveaux types de données...), et aussi nous permettre de mettre à jour les données plus facilement à l'avenir. ## Résultats : - Réduction de la première charge initiale pour les formes des communes (PMTiles) - Nous pouvons garder la taille des données de pollution très petite (code INSEE de la commune + prélèvement). Dans le futur, nous pourrons facilement remplacer les données par un serveur backend, pour interroger les états de pollution par année et par type. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49ac404f-fd64-49dc-93c4-bff452f1ec94 👀 Preview: https://13-pollution-eau-csv.vercel.app/ ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **Nouvelles Fonctionnalités** - Lecture et traitement d'un fichier CSV pour intégrer des données de qualité de l'eau et les afficher dynamiquement. - Amélioration de l'interactivité de la carte avec des effets au survol et une interface de personnalisation visuelle. - **Changements de Configuration et Dépendances** - Adaptation de la configuration pour permettre une prévisualisation sans interruption malgré certains avertissements. - Mise à jour et ajout de dépendances afin de soutenir les nouvelles fonctionnalités.

vulnerabilities.
-->

#### What it does

When frontend and main VS Code extensions load together, Theia creates two extension host instances to manage different kinds of extensions. Each will register the extensions' contributed debug adapter configuration providers with incremented handles.

In cases of handle collisions during the registration of debug configurations, Theia adjusts the handle of incoming providers. However, this adjustment causes issues as the extension host no longer associates the new handle with the original ID.

For instance, if the main VSIX contributes two debuggers assigned handles `0` and `1`, and the web VSIX contributes a debugger with a colliding handle `0`, Theia changes the web provider's handle to `2`. Subsequently, when starting a debug session, the main extension attempts to resolve handle `2`, but the frontend extension host only recognizes the initial configuration.

This commit addresses the issue by storing the original handle of the debug adapter configuration. During handle ID lookups, it will reference the originally assigned handle instead of the adjusted one, ensuring proper resolution and functionality across both extension host instances.

Ref: eclipse-theia/theia#13196

}

author: webalexeu
body:
## Describe your changes
- The registry key that is currently used to check if the client is in GPO mode or not is not correct. You can have DNSClient key present if you define other DNS settings by GPO (Ex: Disable Netbios, disable mutlicast, ...) but not using GPO to configure Nrpt policies.
- When client is in GPO mode, there is no need to push the local policy configuration as this entry will be discared. The way of Microsoft to check if there is NRPT settings configured by GPO is to check the DnsPolicyConfig key is present (That's why it's coherent to check that key and not the DNSClient key)

> If any NRPT settings are configured in domain Group Policy, then all local Group Policy NRPT settings are ignored
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-r2-and-2012/dn593632(v=ws.11)

## Issue ticket number and link
Partial fix https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/issues/3332

author: m-vo
body:
Fixes https://github.com/contao/docs/issues/1549

This PR…
* drops the existing bundle templates*
* directly renders the new ones if and only if a legacy one does not exist (BC)
* adds a conditional extends tag for the legacy bundle templates layout for all error templates**.

This way you can still have a `templates/bundles/ContaoCoreBundle/Error/layout.html.twig` and/or a `templates/bundles/ContaoCoreBundle/Error/service_unavailable.html.twig` etc.

*) For now except the legacy 'layout' base template, because otherwise adjusting _just_ a child template and extending from the legacy one would not work anymore.

**) This would technically work by not specifying the second argument (the new template), because currently the old one always exists. But this is IMHO cleaner, as it allows us to drop the old layout template without breaking anything but the above use case. Plus - when we remove the BC layer - the correct name is already in there.

author: parkhanbum
body:
In the previous code, it specified the destination vector as the getShuffleCost argument. Because the shuffle mask specifies the indices of the two vectors specified as elements, the maximum value is twice the size of the source vector. This causes a problem if the destination vector is smaller than the source vector and specify an index in the mask that exceeds the size of the destination vector.

Fix the problem by correcting the previous code, which was using wrong argument in the Cost calculation.

Fixed https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/130250

PHP version 8.3.13 is vulnerable to CVE-2024-11236, which exists in versions >= 8.3.0, < 8.3.14.

The vulnerability was found in the [National Vulnerability Database (NVD)](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-11236) based on the CPE cpe:2.3:a:php:php with NVD severity: Critical.

This vulnerability has a known exploit available. Source: [Github](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-5hqh-c84r-qjcv).

The vulnerability can be remediated by updating PHP to 8.3.14 or higher. PHP 8.3.16 is the latest version.

author: wertik
body:
Hey :wave:

Add a `smash-attack` flag to prevent smash attacks with a mace.

Smash attacks allow players to knock others out of regions. Due to the fact that Paper nor Spigot currently call a knockback event that could get cancelled, the only way to prevent that seems to be [`EntityAttemptSmashAttackEvent`](https://jd.papermc.io/paper/1.21.4/io/papermc/paper/event/entity/EntityAttemptSmashAttackEvent.html) that's only present in Paper, hence a check for its presence on load is required.

Once the knockback event gets implemented, having a `knockback` flag will be more reasonable. I'll be raising an issue on the PaperMC github to implement this.

Note that disabling animal harm in the region would prevent the use of a mace on them, but hostile mobs would still pose a problem.

The flag was implemented on request. It's up to the author whether they see it as a valid addition for this plugin or find inspiration for a different approach. For anyone encountering the same protection exploit, there's my fork to use.

author: jasondsmith72
body:
## Problem
The `simple-install.bat` script creates a malformed JSON file for `claude_desktop_config.json` which causes Claude Desktop to show this error:

```
Could not load app settings
There was an error reading or parsing claude_desktop_config.json: Unexpected token ',', 'mcps'... is not valid JSON
```

This happens because batch files with `echo` can introduce inconsistent line endings and whitespace that cause JSON parsing errors.

## Solution
This PR provides multiple improvements to fix the issue:

### 1. Improved `simple-install.bat`:
- Now creates automatic backups of existing config files with date and time stamp
- Uses PowerShell's `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` method with UTF-8 encoding for clean JSON creation
- Added JSON validation to verify the file is valid before completing installation
- Shows backup location in completion message

### 2. New `fix-config.bat`:
- A dedicated tool to fix corrupt configuration files
- Doesn't require reinstallation of the whole package
- Makes backups of existing config files
- Works with both system-wide and portable Node.js installations

### 3. New `emergency-fix.bat`:
- Ultra-simple script that resets the config to a minimal valid state
- For users experiencing the "Unexpected token" error who need immediate fixes
- Creates backups before making changes
- Provides clear instructions on next steps

## Benefits
- Fixes "Option one installer has an error" mentioned in the README
- Uses the same reliable JSON handling as the PowerShell script but still allows batch file usage
- Adds validation to confirm the JSON is valid before completing installation
- Provides multiple recovery options for different scenarios
- Preserves user configurations with automatic backups

## Testing
- Tested on Windows 10 and confirmed this generates valid JSON that Claude can parse correctly
- Verified that the emergency fix resolves the "Unexpected token" error

Updated the `initState` method to initialize the location service and subscribe to the position stream. Modified the `build` method to use the last known position for the map center and display the user's route on the map. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdR17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdR35-L36) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdR102-R112) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdL126) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdL135-R144) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdL223-L231) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdL249-R250) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdR262-R296) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdL273-R330) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdR346-R418) [[11]](diffhunk://#diff-b0511e86f9fac90200a78ac64abe8d98ababb85f18f1ddccff3b420eabb1becdL339-L367)

author: ldematte
body:
Using ASM CheckClassAdapter was key to diagnose the issue we had with incorrect signatures for some check methods. 
In this PR I polished up the code I used to pinpoint the issue, and made it available via a system property so it can be turned on if we need it (and it's always on for Entitlements IT tests too).

It is also turned on in case we get VerifyErrors during retransformClasses early in the Entitlement agent bootstrap: `retransformClasses` runs in the native part of the JVM, so the `VerifyError` it produces is not so readable (e.g. it lacks a full stack trace and a description); in case this happens, we re-apply the transformation with verification turned on to get a meaningful error before dying.

author: hugotiburtino
body:
Unfortunatelly the solution with git lfs (see #46 and #47) is not quite practical regarding creating docker image.
Git Lfs does not automatically download the file and it only works when pulling the code. 
Dockerfile would then have to have a git clone, instead of using the file that is in the source code itself.
 
So, the solution of compressing the dump file seems more simple: zipping/unzipping files is more usual than using git lfs,
and it is a dependency less.

author: carloslavilla
body:
Added functionality for the LLM service where we will delegate the creation of the distractors. This implementation will return an array containing 3 incorrect answers provided the correct answer. So for example, for the request:

`http://localhost:8003/generateIncorrectOptions`
And within the body of the request we have:
```
{
    "model": "empathy",
    "apiKey": "apiKey", // To be replaced by our API key
    "correctAnswer": "Cote D'Ivoire"
}
```
An example response is:
```
{
    "incorrectOptions": [
        [
            "Nigeria",
            "Togo",
            "Mali"
        ]
    ]
}
```

Note that the endpoint is likely to change due to another issue where they are depending on this implementation, see on:

-  #41

## 🔍 Overview
This PR implements a complete barcode management system for CINERENTAL's equipment inventory, including API endpoints, frontend integration, and business logic for generating, validating, and managing equipment barcodes. The implementation follows industry best practices for barcode generation, format validation, and checksum calculation. Additionally, this PR includes significant code quality improvements to address duplication issues identified by SonarQube.

## Key Changes

<details>
<summary>🔢 Barcode Generation System</summary>

- Implemented centralized barcode generation using GlobalBarcode model
- Created BarcodeService with validation, generation, and checksum verification functions
- Added barcode preview functionality before equipment creation
- Implemented barcode regeneration for existing equipment items
- Added barcode format validation and uniqueness verification
- Implemented numeric barcode format with checksum validation
</details>

<details>
<summary>🔄 Code Refactoring and Model Restructuring</summary>

- Implemented centralized barcode generation with GlobalBarcode model
- Reorganized model imports to eliminate circular dependencies
- Created new directory structure for models (core, mixins, base_models)
- Restructured web routes into modular components
- Implemented proper dependency injection in services
</details>

<details>
<summary>🖥️ Frontend Integration</summary>

- Updated equipment templates to display barcode information
- Added user interface for barcode management
- Implemented barcode copy functionality on button click
- Improved UI for booking and client pages
- Added validation for replacement cost input
- Enhanced error handling and user notifications
</details>

<details>
<summary>🚀 API Enhancements</summary>

- Added endpoints for barcode generation and validation
- Implemented API for barcode preview functionality
- Added endpoint for equipment barcode regeneration
- Added endpoints for retrieving equipment status timeline and bookings
- Improved error handling and input validation
</details>

<details>
<summary>📝 Code Quality Improvements</summary>

- Restructured model mixins to eliminate 87.5% code duplication
- Created utilities module for web routes with common template data transformation functions
- Refactored equipment routes to reduce duplication by 17.1%
- Improved code organization by separating TimestampMixin and SoftDeleteMixin
- Added backward compatibility through strategic re-exports
- Implemented consistent approach for template data preparation across all route modules
- Enhanced type annotations and error handling in utility functions
</details>

<details>
<summary>📊 Testing and Documentation</summary>

- Updated integration tests for the new barcode system
- Updated unit tests for BarcodeService
- Fixed syntax errors in test files
- Updated fixtures to reflect model changes
- Improved test configuration and event loop handling
- Enhanced testing documentation
</details>

## 💡 Impact
These changes significantly improve:

- **Inventory Management**: Complete system for generating and managing equipment barcodes
- **Data Integrity**: Proper barcode format validation and uniqueness verification
- **User Experience**: Intuitive frontend for barcode operations
- **Maintainability**: Well-structured code with improved dependency management

body:
## Description
Enable hermetic builds: 
1. ui-logging-pf4 (logging-view-plugin v6.0, supports Patternfly4)  
    - prefetch: go.mod, npm 
2. ui-logging (logging-view-plugin v6.1, supports Patternfly5) 
    - prefetch: go.mod, npm 
3. ui-dashboards 
    - prefetch: go.mod, npm 
4. ui-troubleshooting-panel
   - prefetch: go.mod, npm 
5. ui-distributed-tracing-pf4 (logging-view-plugin v0.3, supports Patternfly4) 
    - prefetch: go.mod, npm 
6. ui-distributed-tracing (logging-view-plugin v0.4, supports Patternfly5) 
     - prefetch: go.mod, npm 
7. perses 
     - prefetch: go.mod, npm 
8. perses-operator 
    - prefetch: go.mod, (*does not have frontend component, no need to prefetch for npm )

### Context
"A hermetic build is a secure, self-contained build process that doesn’t depend on anything outside of the build environment. This means that it does not have network access, is not vulnerable to external influences, and cannot fetch dependencies at run time. Instead, you must declare all required resources and dependencies in your build definition.

In Konflux, you can block network access to the build process and run a hermetic build by setting the hermetic parameter in your pipeline definition file to true. This means that you must fetch all dependencies before the build can start. " 
https://konflux.pages.redhat.com/docs/users/how-tos/configuring/hermetic-builds.html (VPN required)

author: thecoderadi
body:
Fix issue: #18 

This pull request introduces a new carousel feature and refactors existing components to improve the user interface. The most important changes include the addition of the `CustomCarousel` component, updates to the `Hero` and `Newest` components to utilize the new carousel, and the creation of a custom hook for the carousel functionality.

### New Carousel Feature:

* `app/components/CustomCarousel.tsx`: Introduced a new `CustomCarousel` component to display products in a carousel format.
* `components/ui/carousel.tsx`: Created a set of carousel components (`Carousel`, `CarouselContent`, `CarouselItem`, `CarouselPrevious`, `CarouselNext`) using `embla-carousel-react` and `embla-carousel-autoplay` for enhanced carousel functionality.

### Component Refactoring:

* `app/components/Hero.tsx`: Updated the `Hero` component to dynamically generate links and refactored the layout for displaying links.
* `app/components/Newest.tsx`: Modified the `Newest` component to use the new `CustomCarousel` instead of a static grid layout.

### Dependency Updates:

* `package.json`: Added `embla-carousel-autoplay` and `embla-carousel-react` dependencies to support the new carousel feature.

author: eed3si9n
body:
Here's a blog post [sudori part 7: client-side run with sbt](https://eed3si9n.com/sudori-part7-client-side-run-with-sbt/)
Ref https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8040
Ref https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/7688
Fixes https://github.com/sbt/sbt/issues/6178

| feature                    | sbt 1.x | sbt 2.x | availability    | console / stdin | JIT perf | isolation |
|----------------------------|:-------:|:-------:|:----------------:|:---------------:|:--------:|:--------:|
| server-side x              |    ✅   |    ✅  |        ❌        |        ⚠️      |     ✅    |   ❌      |
| client-side x              |    ❌   |    ✅  |        ✅        |        ✅      |     ⚠️    |     ✅    |
| persistent worker (planned)|    ❌   |   ✅   |        ✅        |        ❌      |     ✅    |     ✅    |


## Problem
`run` task has been emulated via function call inside of a sandboxed classloader, and blocking the command processing of sbt server loop. This poses isolation and availability issues.

## Solution
As a follow-up to  https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8040, this implements client-side run where the server creates a sandbox environment, and sends the information to the client, and the client forks a new JVM to perform the run. The client-side behavior has been implemented in sbtn side already.

body:
**FE7. De server en clients moeten onderbrekingen in de verbinding kunnen detecteren en herstellen zonder corrupte of onvolledige bestanden achter te laten. (Timer inbouwen die .part bestanden 1x in de zoveel tijd opruimt)**
_De eis komt voort uit de behoefte om te voorkomen dat er gedeeltelijke of corrupte bestanden achterblijven wanneer een upload mislukt of abrupt wordt geannuleerd en later niet wordt hervat._

Deze implementatie bereid het hervatten van upload voor, dit is een nog te implementeren functionaliteit.

Een partial is pas geschikt voor verwijdering wanneer deze niet in gebruik is en wanneer deze niet meer is aangepast na een bepaalde tijd.(huidig staat deze tijd op 10 minuten, eenvoudig aan te passen door verandering van variabel)

**Toevoegingen**
- import time om in de zoveel tijd de zaak op te schonen
- clean stale partial files functionaliteit om oude files te deleten
- start stale files clean up, instantieren van clean stale partial files in een eigen thread(tijden runtime up houden om periodiek te kunnen checken)
- aanroepen, van start stale files clean up, bij server opstart

**Aandachtspunten:**
- niet uitgebreid getest, simpele tests lijken te werken, zie eerdere PR van FE7
- Voor een correcte werking mag .partial geen geaccepteerde file extensie zijn voor een gefinaliseerde upload

**Mogelijke uitbreiding:**
- tijdelijke files buiten de gesyncte mappen bewaren.
- Wanneer een tijdelijke file/upload compleet is van de tijdelijek map naar de productie/sync map verplaatsen.
- Het scheiden van logica voor alle functionaliteit zou het makkelijker maken om verder te implementeren.
- Doormiddel van hashing zouden andere randzaken afgevangen moeten worden, er zal nog wel gekeken moeten worden hoe een upload hervat kan worden in combinatie met hashing.

**Bij het testen zijn de volgende zaken naar voor gekomen die voornamelijk buiten de scope van de FE vallen:**
- Naamswijziging niet gesynct: Bij een naamswijziging op de client wordt deze wijziging niet gesynchroniseerd met de server.
- Waarom alleen hashbestand op server? De reden dat er alleen een hashbestand op de server staat, is nog onduidelijk.
- Sync bij afgebroken verbinding: Wanneer een verbinding afbreekt, wordt de synchronisatie niet hersteld, hoewel de notificationstream opnieuw online komt wanneer de verbinding hersteld is.
- Onbegrijpelijk errorbericht: De foutmelding over bestandsoverdracht is onduidelijk, maar de bestanden lijken wel correct gesynchroniseerd.
- Time-out error: Na ontvangst van een bestand treedt er een time-out error op, maar de bestanden lijken correct te zijn gesynchroniseerd.
- Er lijkt een delete plaats te vinden na het uploaden van een bestand in combinatie met de hashing.
- Hash alleen bij succesvolle upload: De hash wordt alleen aangemaakt wanneer een upload succesvol is.
- Hash mismatch bij grote bestanden: Er komt een hash mismatch bij grote bestandssynchronisaties.

The viewassist_countdown custom element has the following attributes
- `expires` - (required datetime) - a datetime that javascript can convert to a JS Date object
- `server_time` (optional boolean, default true) - define if the countdown uses server time to compare the expires
- `show_negative` (optional boolean, default true) - define if should display expired or negative countdown
- `no_timer_text` (optional string, default '') - define text to display if expiry is 0
- `expired_text` (optional stinrg, default '') - define text to display when timer has expired (if show negative is false)

author: mordante
body:
The followup paper P3235R3 which is voted in as a DR changes the names foo_locking to foo_buffered. These changes have been applied in this patch.

Before
-------------------------------------------------------
Benchmark             Time             CPU   Iterations
-------------------------------------------------------
printf             71.3 ns         71.3 ns      9525175
print_string        226 ns          226 ns      3105850
print_stack         232 ns          232 ns      3026498
print_direct        530 ns          530 ns      1318447

After
-------------------------------------------------------
Benchmark             Time             CPU   Iterations
-------------------------------------------------------
printf             70.6 ns         70.6 ns      9789585
print_string        222 ns          222 ns      3147678
print_stack         227 ns          227 ns      3084767
print_direct        474 ns          474 ns      1472786

Note: The performance of libc++'s std::print is still extemely slow compared to printf. Based on P3107R5 std::print should outperform printf. The main culprit is the call to isatty, which is resolved after implementing
LWG4044  Confusing requirements for std::print on POSIX platforms

Implements
- P3107R5 - Permit an efficient implementation of ``std::print``

Implements parts of
- P3235R3 std::print more types faster with less memory

Fixes: #105435
